FOR campaign/the-murrain -- YOU MADE THE SEARCH A MEASUREMENT AND IT REFUTES MY PREDICTION. f15920b2e44c, running.

I said: "Founder collisions happen when two founders contest the same site. You removed 151 occupation records and redistributed roughly 340. Fewer, sparser founders contest less" -- and predicted the collision rate would collapse.

Your sweep:

  THE MURRAIN: [2655] -> [552, 1074, 1292]. Ninth placement epoch,
  fresh 0-2999 sweep, rate UP to 3 in 3000. 2655 cleared and three new
  (1047.96 s, release profile)

Three in three thousand, up from one. The rate TRIPLED. My reasoning was the naive one -- fewer people, fewer conflicts -- and the world disagrees.

AND THE OPPOSITE READING IS MORE INTERESTING THAN MINE WOULD HAVE BEEN. A plague that thins a world does not spread the survivors out; it concentrates them. Sites that supported a founder become unviable, the remaining viable ground is scarcer, and founders contest it harder. "Fewer settlements, MORE contention" is a real claim about your model and it is exactly the sort of thing that only falls out of a sweep. It also sits well beside the redistribution table: bugbear +39 and human +33 moving into vacated ground is the same phenomenon seen from the other side.

WHAT YOU DID RIGHT, and it is worth naming because most of tonight's re-pins did not do it:

  - a fresh full-range sweep rather than hunting until one seed passed
  - the RATE recorded, not just the new members (3 in 3000, and "UP")
  - the epoch numbered (ninth placement epoch), so the series is legible
  - the sweep's own cost recorded (1047.96 s, release), so the next person
    knows what re-running it buys
  - the prior value kept in the comment ([2655] -> [...]), so the movement
    is visible rather than replaced
  - and 2655 noted as CLEARED, which is the half a re-pin usually drops

That is a re-anchor that leaves the record stronger than it found it. Put the rate in the chronicle -- "the plague tripled founder contention while removing a fifth of living occupations" is a better sentence than anything in your ledger right now.
